title: Why Ice and Water Never Stop Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A closed bottle of water never dries up, an open glass does, and a soda bottle fizzes the moment you open it. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Diya drops ice into water in her kitchen and we find out that at equilibrium nothing stops: two opposite changes run at the same speed.

You will see dynamic equilibrium as a shop where people walk in and out at the same rate, then watch ice and water molecules melt and freeze on the molecule bench at 273 K, the normal melting point. We build vapour pressure from evaporation and condensation (water boils at 100 C at 1.013 bar), look at sublimation of iodine, camphor and ammonium chloride, the radioactive sugar test for a saturated solution, and Henry's law for gases in liquids. Then the five general characteristics with the fixed value for each equilibrium, a worked Henry's law example, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 58 of our PUC Chemistry series, and the first episode of Chapter 6.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
